newsitem.title: UK: UK shares up, hold gains ahead of Wall St start.
newsitem.headline: UK shares up, hold gains ahead of Wall St start.

text.p: British shares held the bulk of their early gains by early afternoon on Monday, expecting a steady start on Wall Street and largely shrugging off weak gilts and sharp falls in continental European shares.
Friday's strength on Wall Street propelled the UK market higher from the outset and by 1310 GMT the FTSE 100 index was up 23.3 points at 4,668.3, pushing towards its record 4,723.7 set on May 16.
Banks led the advance as a bout of bid speculation lifted NatWest, up 18p at 798-1/2, and gainers overall were in a two-to-one majority.

"All the banks have been firm and the rest of the market followed," said a dealer at one top investment bank. "There are really no sellers around...I can see the FTSE closing about 35 points higher so long as Wall Street doesn't come off."

However, he said the market's gains had been made in relatively thin trade. Volume reached 431 million by 1317 GMT, boosted by 28 million in penny stock Dragon Oil and 24 million Cable & Wireless, which eased as enthusiasm waned for its China Telecom deal.
"Volume is very thin, we are just sitting here waiting for the day to end," the trader said.
NatWest led the bank sector higher, after a report in the Sunday Times said there was pressure from its major institutional shareholders for a bid or merger.

The newspaper said a deal could value the underperforming stock at 10 stg. Separately, the Daily Telegraph said Abbey's chief executive had supported a merger with NatWest but had backed down after resistance from the rest of the company's board.
Meanwhile, gilts were unsupportive, declining after higher-than-expected producer prices in May. Industrial production and manufacturing output in April were also stronger than forecast.
The figures were seen as supporting the Bank of England's decision to raise interest rates last week. The September long gilt future was down 17/32 to 113-17/32 by 1340 GMT.

Growing uncertainties over the move towards European monetary union helped send shares sharply lower in continental Europe, with the CAC-40 down 41.25 to 2,678.00 and Germany's DAX-30 down 27.86 to 3,667.43.
"France and Germany look politically a bit wobbly and the UK is a safe haven," said one trader.
